definitions.rated: Institutions with a 3-year rate in the window: a campus listed by DOE in each of its years, a link campus in a U.S. state, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico or the U.S. Virgin Islands (config.py US_STATES), a rate denominator (on-campus FTE, pooled FTE added) of at least minFte in each year, and no rule (hospital, medical, listed, merger, family, shared_pooled, shared_campus) in any year. The window files list exactly these.
definitions.listed: Rated institutions without a reason (why) whose expected count at the national rate is at least lists.minExpected: the members of the national ordered list.
definitions.stateLists: Per state, the national list's members in that state; a state list is published (positions and ranges within the state) when it has at least lists.stateMinMembers members.
definitions.withFte: Institution-years whose link campus is in US_STATES with a rate denominator of at least minFte, rules included (single years).
definitions.ratedYears: Of withFte, those with a single-year rate: no rule, and not a year of skipYears.

offenses.description: The 11 criminal offenses added up: murder, negligent manslaughter, rape, fondling, incest, statutory rape, robbery, aggravated assault, burglary, motor vehicle theft and arson. VAWA offenses, arrests and disciplinary referrals are not included.

Murder and non-negligent manslaughter, rape, robbery and aggravated assault: the offenses the FBI counts as violent crime (Crime in the United States). Fondling, incest and statutory rape are not included.
Burglary, motor vehicle theft and arson: the offenses the FBI counts as property crime (Crime in the United States), without larceny-theft, which Clery does not collect.

Every category added up: criminal offenses, VAWA offenses (domestic violence, dating violence, stalking), arrests and disciplinary referrals for drug, liquor and weapons law violations. These are different kinds of counts: arrests and referrals count people, not incidents, and an incident of dating violence, domestic violence or stalking can also be counted as a criminal offense. High totals often reflect drug and alcohol enforcement, not violent crime.
The willful (non-negligent) killing of one human being by another
The killing of another person through gross negligence
Penetration, no matter how slight, of the vagina or anus with any body part or object, or oral penetration by a sex organ of another person, without the consent of the victim
The touching of the private body parts of another person for the purpose of sexual gratification, without the consent of the victim
Sexual intercourse between persons who are related to each other within the degrees wherein marriage is prohibited by law
Sexual intercourse with a person who is under the statutory age of consent
The taking or attempting to take anything of value from the care, custody, or control of a person or persons by force or threat of force
An unlawful attack by one person upon another for the purpose of inflicting severe or aggravated bodily injury
The unlawful entry of a structure to commit a felony or a theft
The theft or attempted theft of a motor vehicle
Any willful or malicious burning or attempt to burn a dwelling house, public building, motor vehicle, or personal property
A felony or misdemeanor crime of violence committed by a current or former spouse or intimate partner
Violence committed by a person who is or has been in a social relationship of a romantic or intimate nature with the victim
Engaging in a course of conduct directed at a specific person that would cause a reasonable person to fear for their safety
Arrests for the violation of laws prohibiting the manufacture, sale, or possession of weapons
Arrests for violations of laws prohibiting the production, distribution, and/or use of controlled substances
Arrests for the violation of state or local laws prohibiting the manufacture, sale, purchase, transportation, or possession of alcoholic beverages
Persons referred for disciplinary action for weapons law violations
Persons referred for disciplinary action for drug law violations
Persons referred for disciplinary action for liquor law violations
